issues.description: Frame carries a live FrameProcessor reference instead of a stable identifier
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame now holds a direct reference to a FrameProcessor in its `service` field. Frames are data — they flow through queues, get logged, potentially serialized, and compared. Embedding a live object means identity-equality (`frame.service == self.strategy.active_service`) is the only thing that works; you cannot log, replay, or persist this frame meaningfully, and any future serialization boundary will break. A string service name or stable id would keep the data structure flat and the comparison obvious. Data dominates: pick the right shape and the algorithm follows.

issues.description: Forward-reference string type on a dataclass field couples frames.py to processor module
issues.detail: The `service: "FrameProcessor"` annotation papers over a circular-import problem by quoting the type. That is a smell that the data structure is in the wrong place or carrying the wrong thing. If `service` were an identifier (str) the import goes away entirely and the frame stays a pure data record. Quoted forward refs in a dataclass that other modules introspect tend to bite later (dataclasses, typing.get_type_hints, pydantic adapters).

issues.description: push_frame logic could be a flat filter rather than nested isinstance branches
issues.detail: The switcher's push_frame is two stateless predicates over the incoming frame: drop-if-handled-request, drop-if-inactive-metadata, else forward. The nested `if isinstance ... if frame.service == ...` reads fine but the shape is a classic Unix filter — input frame in, optional frame out, no state changes. A small guard list or early-return chain keeps that shape obvious and makes future suppressions (there will be more) drop in without growing the if-tree.

issues.description: STTService and MockMetadataService duplicate the same handling pattern
issues.detail: Both `STTService.process_frame` and the test's `MockMetadataService.process_frame` implement the identical sequence: push metadata, then forward the request frame. That duplication is fine for two callers, but every future service that emits ServiceMetadataFrame will copy the same three lines. A tiny mixin or a default base-class handler (`async def _handle_request_metadata(self, frame, direction)`) would let each service supply just `_push_*_metadata()` and stop the copy-paste before it spreads.

issues.description: Comparison by object identity is undocumented and fragile
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on FrameProcessor not overriding `__eq__`, which today means identity comparison. That's the right behavior here, but it is implicit. Either use `is` to make the intent explicit (identity, not equality), or switch to comparing stable identifiers. `is` is one character shorter and says exactly what's meant.

review.summary: The rename and the targeting mechanism are sound — the old global suppression was the bug, and routing the request to one named service is the right fix. The wart is the data structure: the frame carries a live FrameProcessor reference, which forces a quoted forward-ref import, makes the frame unserializable/unloggable, and pins the comparison to object identity. A string service name or id would make the frame a plain data record and the algorithm self-evident. The push_frame filter and the per-service handler are also begging to be factored into smaller composable pieces before a third service copies the pattern. SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE on the overall shape; WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE on the `service: FrameProcessor` field.
